newsitem.title: USA: AFTER THE BELL - IBM trades lower at 168.
newsitem.headline: AFTER THE BELL - IBM trades lower at 168.

text.p: International Business Machines Corp was trading at 168 in after-hours trading on Tuesday, 1-3/8 lower than at its close on the New York Stock Exchange, traders said Tuesday.
"It's choppy," said one trader, refering to the share price's movement.
After the close, IBM reported fourth-quarter earnings of $3.93 a share against $3.09 for the same period last year. First Call's analysts' consensus was $3.88 a share.
"I can't see how they'd punish them with these numbers, but any stock that's been this straight up can see some profit taking," said Arnie Owen, director of equities at Kaufman Brothers.
Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood, said he did not see the results affecting the company's share price very much.

"I don't think it's going to have a giant impact on the stock one way or another," he said. "But I think it may cause a brief period of selling because Wall Street (sells) on that kind of news. ...I don't get the feeling that we're going to get more exuberance in the price."
A Wall Street technology stock trader agreed. "There is nothing to drive the stock," he said.
Another trader covering the after-hours session later said U.S. Robotics was trading at 74-1/4 against its close of 73-5/8 on the Nasdaq.
After the close, U.S. Robotics posted first-quarter earnings of $0.72 a share against $0.45 in the year-ago period.
The New York Stock Exchange said volume in the first session was 7,200 shares, compared with 92,800 on Monday, while volume in the second session reached 217,900, compared with 277,900.
